extra.message: User input from form.registration_code.data is passed as the `code` parameter and concatenated directly into a raw SQL query via f-string inside text(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g., ' OR 1=1 --) to bypass registration code validation or extract data.

User input from request.args.get('search') is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE clause via text(f"text like '%{search_param}%'"). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL to read or modify data in the database.

request.path is interpolated into a string passed to render_template_string(). Since request.path is user-controlled, an attacker can inject Jinja2 template expressions (e.g., {{config}} or {{().__class__.__mro__}}) to achieve Server-Side Template Injection and remote code execution.

pickle.loads() is called on the base64-decoded value of the user-controlled 'preferences' cookie. Since this runs in a @app.before_request handler, it executes on every request. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload in the cookie to achieve remote code execution on the server.

urlopen() is called with a user-controlled URL from the ImageForm. An attacker can supply internal network URLs (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ for cloud metadata), file:// URLs for local file reads, or any arbitrary URL to make the server perform requests on their behalf.

The note.text field is rendered with the | safe filter, which disables Jinja2 auto-escaping. Since note text is user-controlled input from the NoteForm, an attacker can store malicious HTML/JavaScript in a note that will execute in any user's browser who views the home page.

The render_table macro is called with safe_columns=['text'], which disables HTML escaping for the note 'text' column. Since note text contains user-controlled input, an attacker can store malicious HTML/JavaScript in a note that will execute when search results are displayed.

The render_table macro is called with safe_columns=['text'], which disables HTML escaping for the note 'text' column. Since note text contains user-controlled input, an attacker can store malicious HTML/JavaScript in a note that will execute when personal notes are displayed.

guess_type(url) determines the MIME type from the URL extension without validating it is an image type. An attacker can provide a URL ending in .html, causing the MIME type to be text/html. The resulting data:text/html;base64,... URI is stored as the profile image and rendered in an <object> tag in the browser, executing arbitrary JavaScript as stored XSS.

The get_personal_notes endpoint accepts a user_id from the URL path without verifying it matches current_user.id. Any authenticated user can view any other user's notes (including private ones) by changing the user_id in the URL (e.g., /accounts/1/notes).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The update_account POST endpoint lacks the @login_required decorator, unlike the GET /account endpoint at line 18. Any unauthenticated user can submit a POST request to /account to modify account data, including email and is_admin fields.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The AccountForm includes an is_admin BooleanField, and the update_account handler applies all form fields (except password) to current_user.__dict__ without authorization checks. A regular user can submit is_admin=True in a POST request to /account to escalate their privileges to admin.

The Flask secret key is hardcoded as 'super secret key'. This key is used to sign session cookies. An attacker who knows this key can forge valid session cookies, impersonate any user (including admins), and bypass authentication entirely.

A static registration code 'a36e990b-0024-4d55-b74a-f8d7528e1764' is hardcoded in the database seed script. Anyone with access to the source code can use this code to register accounts without authorization.

The delete_note endpoint deletes any note by ID without verifying that the note belongs to the current user or that the current user is an admin. Any authenticated user can delete any note in the system by providing the note ID in the URL.

SQLAlchemy engine is created with echo=True, which logs all SQL statements including parameter values to stdout/stderr. This can expose sensitive data such as passwords, registration codes, and note contents in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
